items.title: OpenAI Considers Pre-IPO Funding Round at More Than $1.2 Trillion Valuation
items.summary: OpenAI has held preliminary talks with investors about a new funding round that would value the ChatGPT maker at more than $1.2 trillion, ahead of a planned IPO next year, capitalizing on demand for its technology after recent model launches.
items.why_it_matters: A $1.2 trillion valuation would make OpenAI one of the most valuable private companies ever, underscoring investor appetite even amid a heated debate about AI safety and a possible bubble.

items.title: Anthropic merges Claude chat and Cowork in one interface
items.summary: Anthropic is merging its Claude chat and Cowork products into a single interface, initially for Pro and Max plan subscribers. Alongside the merge, Anthropic launched Docs and Slides, new tools that let users create documents and presentations directly through Claude chats, which can then be exported, edited, and shared.
items.why_it_matters: It brings Claude's feature set closer to Google Workspace and Gemini, a direct play for everyday productivity users beyond coding and research tasks.

items.title: EU Unveils Social Media Curbs for Kids and Ban on Users Under 13
items.summary: The European Union is working to ban social media for children under 13 and restrict the use of technology and AI services, including chatbots, for older children, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced in her annual address. Von der Leyen described AI as the 'second tipping point of our time' after climate change.
items.why_it_matters: It's one of the most concrete regulatory moves yet specifically targeting how minors can use AI chatbots, and could set a template other jurisdictions follow.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI want to embed safety evaluators. Will they really be independent?
items.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI are proposing to embed independent safety evaluators inside their AI labs, giving outside researchers unprecedented access to monitor development. Researchers welcome the access but warn meaningful oversight will require real transparency and independence, and likely regulation eventually. Anthropic's head of public policy separately said AI companies can't be expected to operate purely on an 'honor code.'
items.why_it_matters: It's the first concrete institutional proposal from two frontier labs to police themselves after days of public sparring over whether AI development needs to slow down.

items.title: Novo Nordisk Will Use Anthropic's Claude for Drug Research
items.summary: Novo Nordisk, the maker of Ozempic, is partnering with Anthropic to use Claude to speed up drug development, as the pharma company works to catch up in the competitive obesity-drug market.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete example of a major pharmaceutical company betting on a frontier AI model to accelerate real drug discovery, not just back-office tasks.

items.title: AI must not outrun safety controls, DeepMind co-founder warns
items.summary: DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg told the FT that AI must not outrun safety controls, speaking as DeepMind launches a new institute to explore the implications of artificial general intelligence. The launch comes amid growing industry calls for a slowdown in frontier AI development.
items.why_it_matters: It shows one of DeepMind's own founders formalizing safety research even as the industry debates whether self-regulation is enough.

items.title: Anthropic lands deal in $31bn datacentre in western Queensland, David Crisafulli says
items.summary: Anthropic has struck a deal to lease the site of its first Australian datacentre in western Queensland, worth about $31.9bn. Queensland premier David Crisafulli described the deal as a 'major win' that will create jobs in the state and add energy capacity to its grid.
items.why_it_matters: It's a major international infrastructure commitment for Anthropic and a sign of how aggressively frontier labs are expanding compute capacity outside the US.

items.title: Introducing System One Models and Jev
items.summary: TypeSafe introduced 'System One Models,' a new category of small, fast models built only to decide, classify, route, or score, plus 'Jev,' a specific model in that category that the company says is more than 100x faster and more than 200x cheaper than small frontier LLMs at these tasks.
items.why_it_matters: It proposes a distinct, much cheaper model category for the simple decision-making tasks that make up a large share of real-world AI agent traffic, rather than routing everything through frontier LLMs.

items.title: Artificial intelligence now beats some of the best human forecasters
items.summary: New reporting finds that AI models now beat some of the best human forecasters, with AI forecasting skill described as increasingly indistinguishable from that of top human 'superforecasters,' though important caveats remain about how reliable and generalizable the results are.
items.why_it_matters: Forecasting ability under uncertainty is a strong real-world test of AI reasoning, well beyond scripted benchmarks.

items.title: Mistral X Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing
items.summary: Mistral is partnering with Mozilla, which will use Mistral's AI models to power Firefox's AI assistant, betting on a browser known for privacy protections to grow Mistral's consumer AI base and reach more users across languages.
items.why_it_matters: It gives Mistral a mainstream distribution channel through Firefox, a rare example of a European AI lab winning a marquee consumer partnership.
